paragraphs: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern is governed by a coalition of the centre-left SPD (S&D) and Die Linke (LEFT) under minister-president Manuela Schwesig, in office since 2017 and re-elected in 2021 on the SPD's best state result since reunification — 39.6%, enough for 34 of 79 seats. The SPD has led every government in the state since 1998.

The contest is between the SPD (S&D) and the AfD (ESN), and polling through 2026 has put them within a point or two of each other in the high thirties. The AfD's rise is the mirror image of the CDU (EPP)'s collapse: the CDU took 13.3% in 2021 and has polled between 6% and 10% since the summer, which would be the worst state-election result in the party's history.

The SPD (S&D) is affiliated with the Party of European Socialists and sits in the S&D group. The CDU (EPP) sits with the European People's Party, Die Linke (LEFT) with the Party of the European Left, Bündnis 90/Die Grünen with the European Green Party in Greens/EFA, and the FDP (RE) with Renew Europe. The AfD's MEPs sit with the far-right Europe of Sovereign Nations (ESN) group.

Nineteen state lists were admitted, carrying 313 candidates. The Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW (NI)) is contesting Mecklenburg-Vorpommern for the first time and has polled at or below the 5% threshold all year; the FDP (RE), which cleared it with 5.8% in 2021, has been prompted for in only some polls and scored 2–3% in those. Die Heimat, the former NPD, and dieBasis both contested 2021 and are not standing again.
